note: Every statement in internal/ that no test executes. An entry states why the block cannot be executed, never that nobody has got round to it: a missing test is a missing test, and belongs in a test file. Enforced by internal/coverageaudit's own test, which fails both when an unlisted statement becomes uncovered and when a listed one becomes covered. Keys are file, enclosing function and the block's own source text, so a line moving does not invalidate an entry but a rewrite does.

exclusions.statement: return nil, fmt.Errorf("strategy: instrument %q: fill %q is %s but proposal %q is %s; a fill in the opposite direction is a different position, not the proposed one", fill.InstrumentID, fill.FillID, fill.Direction, fill.ProposalID, pending.direction)
exclusions.reason: The Baseline is long-only: event.DirectionLong is the only direction FillPayload.Validate, TradeProposalPayload.Validate and CampaignOpenedPayload.Validate accept, and a Campaign's own direction is only ever set from an accepted fill. The comparison therefore cannot differ today. It is kept, not deleted, because the rule it states is about reconciliation rather than about the payload contract — a fill in the opposite direction is a different position, not a variant of the same one — and it must already be in place on the day shorts are added rather than being remembered then. This entry becomes reachable, and must move to a test, the moment a second direction is accepted anywhere.

exclusions.statement: return nil, fmt.Errorf( "strategy: applied %d drawdown steps in one account snapshot observation without terminating; this indicates a defect in the drawdown ladder, not a legitimate market condition", i)
exclusions.reason: The Drawdown Ladder's own asymptote check, a few statements above, refuses a ladder whose steps do not converge; with a converging ladder the loop terminates in at most as many steps as the ladder has rungs, far below the cap. Kept as a bound on memory so that a future change to either the ladder or the asymptote check cannot silently reintroduce an unbounded append.
